2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the writ-petition was filed by the respondent alleging, that holding No. 2 of Joginagar, Dhaka originally belonged to one Krista Mohan Das having 8 annas share, which he transferred to respondent-writ-petitioner, by registered kabala with delivery of possession. While purchaser Abdur Rahman was in possession the same was recorded in his name during SA operation in SA Khatian No. 194 and SA Plot No. 772. Abdur Rahman was a Bangladeshi national who was all along residing in the aforesaid holding with other members of his family. While Abdur Rahman was in exclusive possession he transferred the case property to the writ-petitioner by way of a registered kabala dated 24-4-1974 and delivered possession who also got his name mutated. Thereafter, the writ petitioner received a notice asking him to vacate the case premises. He then instituted Title Suit No. 57 of 1976 in the 6th Court of Munsif, Dhaka for permanent injunction restraining the Secretary, Ministry of Works and Urban. Development and others for evicting him from the case property and disturbing his possession and while the suit was pending with an order of injunction in favour of the plaintiff-writ-petitioner Ordinance LV of 1976 come into force on 17th July, the order of injunction passed earlier became ineffective. Thereafter, the writ-petitioner filed application to the Secretary, Ministry of Works for releasing the property which was enlisted as Abandoned Property but in the meantime the petitioner was evicted from the case property. The petitioner then moved the Court of Settlement in Settlement Case No. 47 of 1987 with a prayer for releasing the property but without success. Then, the writ-petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 1413 of 1988 before the High Court Division and the Rule was made absolute on 25-7-1996. 

 3. The facts alleged on behalf of the respondent, inter alia, are that the lands comprising an area of 0.0114 aujutangsha, now holding No. 2 Joginagar lane under Police Station Sutrapur, Dhaka originally belonged to Kritis Mohan Das having his 16 annas title and possession therein who sold the same to Lolit Mohan Das son to Kailash Chandra Das by a registered sale deed on 9-11-1904 corresponding to 18th Kartic 1311 BS and made over possession to him. While the said Lolit Mohan Das in possession the preparation of CS Khatian started and it was recorded in his name in the CS Khatian with a pucca bari being Plot No. 156 in Khatian No. 14170 and later on Khatian No. 143 as in the meantime he made some pucca construction. Lolit Mohan Das died leaving behind his only son who sold the property to one Abdur Rahman by a registered deed dated 29-6-1962 at a valuable consideration. While Abdur Rahman is in possession his name was duly recorded in SA Plot No. 772 of SA Khatian No. 194 under mutation. While Abdur Rahman was in exclusive possession of the said holding No. 2 Joginagar Lane also known as Ganga Ram Shaha Lane transferred the said property in question to the respondent by registered deed of sale dated 24-4-1974 and made over possession of the same to him. After purchase, Md Mohiuddin got his name mutated in respect of the case property and has been in possession of the said holding in question with the members of his family. Suddenly, he received a notice under Memo No. 10/3m-100/75/110 dated 5-2-1976 addressed under the name of the Section officer of the Ministry of Works and Urban Development, Section X, of the Government of Bangladesh directing the respondent addressing as a possession to deliver the possession of the holding within 30 days of the receipt of the notice. After receiving the notice dated 5-2-1976 the respondent was moving from door to door to get released his house from the list of abandoned property but with no favourable result.
